about: Sauvage Distillery was founded in 2017 in Charlotteville, a hamlet in Schoharie County between the Catskills and the Mohawk Valley. Its founder and CEO, Ilio Mavlyanov, began in nearby Oneonta making sparkling cider and wine with local orchards, and the distillery started with a 150-gallon still that turned leftover cider juice into spirit. In 2020 it moved to a 22,000-square-foot distillery on a 25-acre property. Its process was developed by distiller Ken Wortz, and today head distiller Jamie Terk, whom he mentored, leads an all-women distilling team.

Upstate Vodka is distilled entirely from New York apples, about 70 to 80 in every bottle, from family orchards in Schoharie County and the Hudson Valley. Varieties such as Spy Gold, Cortland, Kingston Black and Liberty each bring a different tannin profile. The juice is fermented with kosher yeast, which takes about three times as long as a grain ferment, then distilled twice in two-column stills of 16 and 18 plates and cut with water from the New York State watershed. It is certified kosher and gluten-free, and its label was designed by the studio Stranger & Stranger.
